text:
maria: Heads up — noticed the deprecation sampling dashboard is missing tenant consent flags for a large slice of traffic. looks like ~20% of sampled v1->v2 probe traffic shows no consent_label in the events :confused:

alex: hmm — that's the dataset we use for regressions right? if consent flag is missing we can't segment for tenants that explicitly opted out

sam: can you paste the query you used? I can try to repro locally

maria: pasted below (quick ad-hoc):
```sql
SELECT tenant_id, sample_rate, consent_flag, route_version, timestamp
FROM deprecation_samples
WHERE timestamp >= now() - interval '7 days'
  AND sample_rate > 0
ORDER BY timestamp DESC
LIMIT 100
```

julian: looks fine. but we changed the client header name in the v2 proxy last month (`x-rw-consent` -> `x-rw-consent-v2`). old telemetry pipeline still reads the old header. so events from proxies that didn't upgrade will have null consent_flag

kevin: oh yeah, I rolled a proxy patch last week that added header normalization but only to the hostpool in eu-west. other pools still emit the old header. ops-bot:deploy-1720 triggered on friday :grimacing:

alex: big question: do we treat missing consent as opt-out or opt-in for dashboard sampling? legal might have a view here

legal: quick note from privacy — defaulting to opt-in for telemetry without explicit consent is risky. for product analytics it's one thing, for anything tied to deprecation decisions we should avoid biasing signals with potentially non-consensual data

sam: ok. practical approach: we can mark those events as "consent_unknown" in the UI and filter them out of the default regression cohort. add an explicit toggle in the dashboard to "include consent_unknown" with a red warning

maria: +1. wants to avoid skewing the A/B. also we need to surface which tenant pools are affected so eng can prioritize the proxy normalization rollouts

julian: I'll open a small follow-up to normalize headers across all hostpools and add a parity test. estimated 2-3 hours to patch + smoke. PR coming

kevin: in parallel we should backfill consent_flag where possible from proxy logs. simple script: join requests and raw_proxy_headers by request_id and copy header -> events column. but cannot backfill for hosts that never emitted the header

alex: dashboard UX: show a new bar in the sampling breakdown: "consent: yes / no / unknown" and a top-level banner when unknown fraction > 5% saying "Telemetry incomplete — sampling may be biased" with a link to runbook

maria: runbook link would be great. can we also expose a per-tenant checkbox to exclude consent_unknown from deprec regressions? some platform teams will want to include everything for load reasons

sam: quick POC: add 2 toggles in the deprec dashboard: 1) "exclude unknown consent" (default true) 2) "treat unknown as opt-in" (danger option with confirmation). store toggle in per-user prefs and per-tenant filters

julian: technical note: toggles are frontend-only for now, but we should persist as route-query params so saved reports behave predictably

ops-bot:log: created issue RW-4687: propagate-consent-header-to-all-hostpools

kevin: action items:
- julian: roll header normalization across hostpools (ETA today)
- kevin: backfill script + quick sanity check (ETA tomorrow)
- sam: dashboard toggle POC (ETA EOD)
- maria: draft runbook + banner copy (ETA EOD)
- legal: review banner copy for privacy-safe wording (ETA tomorrow)

alex: also audit quota attribution — if unknown consent tenants are counted in deprecation sample quotas we might be double-billing sample storage. we should treat consent_unknown as not billable for deprecation telemetry until we have opt-in

legal: agree on billing deferral until consent is resolved. we'll need a comms note for customers affected

maria: I'll coordinate comms with growth once we have the hostpool fix and a backfill plan

sam: any objections to ship the dashboard banner + exclude_unknown default immediately? it's a low-risk UI change and reduces confusion for users

alex: no objections. do it. please add a short changelog entry in the console release notes so customer success isn't blindsided

maria: cool. I'll update the thread with PR links and the runbook once ready. thanks all :thumbsup:
